subject: Architecture
title: Urban Heat Islands: Cities That Cook
description: A short lesson to help you apply Urban Heat Islands: Cities That Cook.

hook.text: Cities can be 10°F hotter than surrounding countryside — concrete, steel, and asphalt absorb and radiate heat.

buildup.text: Dark roofs, parking lots, and roads soak up sunlight. At night, they release stored heat instead of cooling down.

discovery.text: Removing trees for development eliminates natural cooling — each mature tree provides the same cooling as ten AC units.

twist.text: Air conditioning exhaust makes it worse — units dump indoor heat outdoors, raising street temperatures further.

climax.text: Los Angeles now paints streets with reflective coating. Cool roofs and urban forests are spreading worldwide.

punchline.text: We built cities that cook themselves. Now we're learning to cool them down.

quiz.question: Why are cities hotter than surrounding rural areas?
options: More people generate body heat in dense populations
Concrete and asphalt absorb and radiate heat instead of cooling
Tall buildings block wind and trap warm air at street level
